dirichlet.name: Dirichlet
dirichlet.description: A quadratic image-fidelity term and Dirichlet gradient penalty define the potential. Backward Euler solves one sparse positive-definite system per update, continuing the occupancy field between observations. The coefficients are fidelity 3 and smoothness 0.008; no momentum variable is used.

ms_split_bregman.name: MS / Split Bregman
ms_split_bregman.description: This solver uses the relaxed two-phase, fixed-intensity Mumford–Shah / Chan–Vese model with TV weight 0.025. It alternates a sparse linear solve, isotropic gradient shrinkage, a box projection, and two Bregman multiplier updates. Primal and dual variables persist across observation stages. Its clock counts iterations.

fixed_at.name: Fixed AT gradient
fixed_at.description: The fixed Ambrosio–Tortorelli potential evolves occupancy u and edge indicator a by gradient flow. Fidelity is 3, field smoothness 0.008, edge cost 0.025, interface scale 0.09, and ellipticity floor 0.004. Configuration dissipation is 0.18. The edge field is projected to [0,1], and energy backtracking controls accepted steps.

untrained_ph.name: Fixed AT / pH
untrained_ph.description: The same fixed AT potential is lifted to phase space with unit mass, momentum damping 2, and configuration dissipation 0.18. Momentum damping is treated implicitly, then configuration advances using the potential force. Energy backtracking applies within each observation stage. Configuration and momentum continue across new measurements.

neural_ph.name: NN + AT / pH
neural_ph.description: The potential is fixed AT plus 0.20 times a nonnegative neural residual potential. An observation-conditioned network supplies positive local mass and damping, while positive configuration dissipation is learned. The canonical pH interconnection remains fixed. Training differentiates through rollouts using received-observation fidelity, late error, settling, and range penalties.

neural_potential.name: Pure NN / gradient
neural_potential.description: A local MLP defines a nonnegative scalar potential from occupancy, received observations, confidence, and spatial differences. This retained baseline advances first-order gradient descent and sets momentum to zero. It contains no explicit AT, TV, or Dirichlet potential. It is separate from the phase-trained NN model.

frozen_nn_ph.name: Frozen GD potential / pH
frozen_nn_ph.description: The exact NN potential learned by the gradient baseline is reused without retraining, then integrated with a phase-space pH flow. Unit mass, damping 2, and configuration dissipation 1 are prescribed. This control isolates the vector-field change from learning different potential weights; the auxiliary AT-edge block remains inert.
frozen_nn_ph.equation: Same frozen V_N; H=V_N+½⟨pᵀp⟩; q̇=p−∇V_N; ṗ=−∇V_N−2p

neural_potential_ph.name: Pure NN / pH
neural_potential_ph.description: The NN learns its scalar potential through phase-space (q,p) rollouts. There is no AT, TV, or Dirichlet potential. Unit mass, damping 2, and configuration dissipation 1 are prescribed, and the canonical interconnection stays fixed. This is an 80-parameter potential at the supplied hidden width 8; its stored edge block is inert.

notes.energy: Energy is model-specific. Compare its evolution within one run.
notes.time: Query progress is aligned across methods. Flow clocks are relaxation units; Split Bregman counts iterations.
notes.projection: The phase portrait is a projection along a shared final-observation direction, not the full field phase space.
notes.data: Precomputed numerical trajectories. Playback speed does not change the integration step or retrain a model.
